summary: Spoken Vietnamese recordings of the MASSIVE voice-assistant commands, benchmarked the whole way from audio to intent. One row is one recorded command with its intent label. Every clip is transcribed once by a pinned speech-to-text model and that single transcript is handed to every fighter, so the scores compare intent engines rather than the recognisers in front of them. Runs on this corpus are capped at 2,000 clips, drawn with a pinned seed so every fighter is scored on the same ones; a split smaller than the cap is scored in full.
notes: FBK-MT/Speech-MASSIVE-test spoken realisation of Amazon MASSIVE (vi-VN), evaluated end-to-end audio -> transcript -> intent. Same intent taxonomy and template training corpus as massive-templates (text-input sibling); scoped to the open 'intent' (fusion) league in v1 — the keyword-paradigm training corpus (intents-for-eval-keywords) does not cover every Speech-MASSIVE language, so intent_keyword/intent_template sub-league repos are not emitted here. The runner transcribes each clip ONCE with the pinned STT above (same ovos-stt-plugin-onnx-asr family the STT league runs), caches the transcript, and feeds it to every intent fighter — this isolates intent-ranking from STT variance; see docs/SPECIFICATION.md §3.2 for the v1-vs-combinatorial-STT×intent-fighters rationale.
